them through life, så wallop efter death. Pom. Wallop. Seems til be
hvad you call yashmak eller I mean kismet. Fate.

Tap. Tap. A stripling, blind, med a tapping cane came taptaptapping ved
Daly’s window hvor a mermaid hair alle streaming (men he couldn’t se)
blew whiffs af a mermaid (blind couldn’t), mermaid, coolest whiff af
alle.

Instruments. A blade af grass, shell af her hands, så blow. Even comb
og tissuepaper you can knock a tune ud af. Molly i her shift i
Lombard gade west, hair ned. I suppose each kind af trade made its
own, don’t you se? Hunter med a horn. Haw. Have you den? _Cloche.
Sonnez la._ Shepherd his pipe. Pwee lille wee. Policeman a whistle.
Locks og keys! Sweep! Four o’clock’s alle’s well! Sleep! alle is lost
nu. Drum? Pompedy. Wait. I ved. Towncrier, bumbailiff. lang John.
Waken den dead. Pom. Dignam. Poor lille _nominedomine._ Pom. It is
musik. I mean af course it’s alle pom pom pom meget meget hvad they call
_da capo._ Still you can hør. As we march, we march along, march
along. Pom.

I must really. Fff. nu if I did that ved a banquet. bare a question af
custom shah af Persia. Breathe a prayer, drop a tear. alle den same he
must have been a bit af a natural ikke til se det var a yeoman cap.
Muffled op. Wonder hvem was that chap ved den grave i den brown macin.
O, den whore af den lane!

A frowsy whore med black straw sailor hat askew came glazily i den
dag along den quay towards Mr Bloom. da first he saw that form
endearing? ja, it is. I føl so lonely. Wet nat i den lane. Horn.
hvem had den? Heehaw shesaw. Off her beat her. hvad is she? Hope she.
Psst! Any chance af your wash. Knew Molly. Had me decked. Stout lady
does be med you i den brown costume. sæt you off your stroke, that.
Appointment we made knowing we’d never, well hardly ever. Too dear too
near til home sweet home. Sees me, does she? Looks a fright i den dag.
ansigt som dip. Damn her. O, well, she has til live som den rest. kig
i her.

i Lionel Marks’s antique saleshop window haughty Henry Lionel Leopold
dear Henry Flower earnestly Mr Leopold Bloom envisaged battered
candlesticks melodeon oozing maggoty blowbags. Bargain: six bob. Might
learn til play. Cheap. Let her pass. Course everything is dear if you
don’t want it. That’s hvad god salesman is. lav you buy hvad he wants
til sell. Chap sold me den Swedish razor he shaved me med. Wanted til
charge me for den edge he gave it. She’s passing nu. Six bob.
Must be den cider eller perhaps den burgund.

Near bronze fra anear near gold fra afar they chinked their clinking
glasses alle, brighteyed og gallant, før bronze Lydia’s tempting
last rose af summer, rose af Castile. First Lid, De, Cow, Ker, Doll, a
fifth: Lidwell, Si Dedalus, Bob Cowley, Kernan og stor Ben Dollard.
Tap. A youth entered a lonely Ormond hall.

Bloom viewed a gallant pictured hero i Lionel Marks’s window. Robert
Emmet’s last words. Seven last words. af Meyerbeer that is.
—True men som you men.
—Ay, ay, Ben.
—Will lift your glass med us.
They lifted.
Tschink. Tschunk.

Tip. An unseeing stripling stood i den dør. He saw ikke bronze. He saw
ikke gold. Nor Ben nor Bob nor Tom nor Si nor George nor tanks nor
Richie nor Pat. Hee hee hee hee. He did ikke se.

Seabloom, greaseabloom viewed last words. Softly. _When my country
takes her place among._
Prrprr.
Must be den bur.
Fff! Oo. Rrpr.

_Nations af den earth._ nej-one behind. She’s passed. _Then og ikke till
så._ Tram kran kran kran. god oppor. kom. Krandlkrankran. I’m
sure it’s den burgund. ja. One, two. _Let my epitaph be._ Kraaaaaa.
_Written. I have._
Pprrpffrrppffff.
_Done._

chapters.title: Episode 12 — Kyklopen
paragraphs:
I was bare passing den tid af dag med gammel Troy af den D. M. P. ved den
corner af Arbour hill der og be damned men a bloody sweep came along
og he near drove his gear ind i my øje. I turned around til let him have
den weight af my tongue da hvem should I se dodging along Stony
Batter only Joe Hynes.

—Lo, Joe, says I. hvordan are you blowing? Did you se that bloody
chimneysweep near shove my øje ud med his brush?
—Soot’s luck, says Joe. hvem’s den gammel ballocks you were talking til?

—gammel Troy, says I, was i den force. I’m på two minds ikke til giv that
fellow i charge for obstructing den thoroughfare med his brooms og
ladders.
—hvad are you doing round those parts? says Joe.

—Devil a meget, says I. der’s a bloody stor foxy thief beyond ved den
garrison church ved den corner af Chicken lane—gammel Troy was bare giving
me a wrinkle om him—lifted any God’s quantity af tea og sugar til
pay three bob a week said han havde a farm i den county ned off a
hop-af-my-thumb ved den name af Moses Herzog over der near Heytesbury
gade.
—Circumcised? says Joe.

—Ay, says I. A bit off den top. An gammel plumber named Geraghty. I’m
hanging på til his taw nu for den past fortnight og I can’t få a
penny ud af him.
—That den lay you’re på nu? says Joe.

—Ay, says I. hvordan are den mighty fallen! Collector af dårlig og doubtful
debts. men that’s den mest notorious bloody robber you’d meet i a
dag’s walk og den ansigt på him alle pockmarks would hold a shower af
rain. _Tell him,_ says he, _I dare him,_ says he, _and I doubledare him
til send you round her again eller if he does,_ says he, _I’ll have him
summonsed op før den court, so I will, for trading without a
licence._ og he efter stuffing himself till he’s fit til burst. Jesus,
I had til laugh ved den lille jewy getting his shirt ud. _He drink me
my teas. He eat me my sugars. Because he nej pay me my moneys?_

for nonperishable goods bought af Moses Herzog, af 13 Saint Kevin’s
parade i den city af Dublin, Wood quay ward, merchant, hereinafter
called den vendor, og sold og delivered til Michael E. Geraghty,
esquire, af 29 Arbour hill i den city af Dublin, Arran quay ward,
gentleman, hereinafter called den purchaser, videlicet, five pounds
avoirdupois af first choice tea ved three shillings og nej pence per
pound avoirdupois og three stone avoirdupois af sugar, crushed
crystal, ved threepence per pound avoirdupois, den said purchaser debtor
til den said vendor af one pound five shillings og sixpence sterling
for value received which amount shall be paid ved said purchaser til said
vendor i weekly instalments hver seven calendar days af three
shillings og nej pence sterling: og den said nonperishable goods shall
ikke be pawned eller pledged eller sold eller otherwise alienated ved den said
purchaser men shall be og remain og be held til be den sole og
exclusive property af den said vendor til be disposed af ved his god
will og pleasure until den said amount shall have been duly paid ved
den said purchaser til den said vendor i den manner herein set forth as
this dag hereby agreed between den said vendor, his heirs, successors,
trustees og assigns af den one part og den said purchaser, his heirs,
successors, trustees og assigns af den other part.
—Are you a strict t.t.? says Joe.
—ikke taking anything between drinks, says I.
—hvad om paying our respects til our friend? says Joe.
—hvem? says I. Sure, he’s ud i John af God’s off his hoved, poor mand.
—Drinking his own stuff? says Joe.
—Ay, says I. Whisky og vand på den brain.
—kom around til Barney Kiernan’s, says Joe. I want til se den citizen.
—Barney mavourneen’s be it, says I. Anything strange eller wonderful, Joe?
—ikke a word, says Joe. I was op ved that meeting i den City Arms.
—hvad was that, Joe? says I.

—Cattle traders, says Joe, om den foot og mouth disease. I want til
giv den citizen den hard word om it.

So we went around ved den Linenhall barracks og den tilbage af den
courthouse talking af one thing eller another. Decent fellow Joe da he
has it men sure som that he never has it. Jesus, I couldn’t få over
that bloody foxy Geraghty, den daylight robber. for trading without a
licence, says he.

i Inisfail den fair der lies a land, den land af holy Michan. der
rises a watchtower beheld af men afar. der sleep den mighty dead as
i life they slept, warriors og princes af high renown. A pleasant
land it is i sooth af murmuring waters, fishful streams hvor sport
den gurnard, den plaice, den roach, den halibut, den gibbed haddock,
den grilse, den dab, den brill, den flounder, den pollock, den mixed
coarse fish generally og other denizens af den aqueous kingdom too
numerous til be enumerated. i den mild breezes af den west og af den
east den lofty trees wave i different directions their firstclass
foliage, den wafty sycamore, den Lebanonian cedar, den exalted
planetree, den eugenic eucalyptus og other ornaments af den arboreal
world med which that region is thoroughly well supplied. Lovely
maidens sit i close proximity til den roots af den lovely trees sang
den mest lovely songs while they play med alle kinds af lovely objects
as for example golden ingots, silvery fishes, crans af herrings, drafts
af eels, codlings, creels af fingerlings, purple seagems og playful
insects. og heroes voyage fra afar til woo them, fra Eblana til
Slievemargy, den peerless princes af unfettered Munster og af Connacht
den bare og af smooth sleek Leinster og af Cruachan’s land og af
Armagh den splendid og af den noble district af Boyle, princes, den
sons af kings.

og der rises a shining palace whose crystal glittering roof is seen
ved mariners hvem traverse den extensive sea i barks built expressly for
that purpose, og thither kom alle herds og fatlings og firstfruits
af that land for O’Connell Fitzsimon takes toll af them, a chieftain
descended fra chieftains. Thither den extremely large wains bring
foison af den fields, flaskets af cauliflowers, floats af spinach,
pineapple chunks, Rangoon beans, strikes af tomatoes, drums af figs,
drills af Swedes, spherical potatoes og tallies af iridescent kale,
York og Savoy, og trays af onions, pearls af den earth, og punnets
af mushrooms og custard marrows og fat vetches og bere og rape og
red green yellow brown russet sweet stor bitter ripe pomellated apples
og chips af strawberries og sieves af gooseberries, pulpy og
pelurious, og strawberries fit for princes og raspberries fra their
canes.

I dare him, says he, og I doubledare him. kom ud her, Geraghty, you
notorious bloody hill og dale robber!

og ved that way wend den herds innumerable af bellwethers og flushed
ewes og shearling rams og lambs og stubble geese og medium steers
og roaring mares og polled calves og longwools og storesheep og
Cuffe’s prime springers og culls og sowpigs og baconhogs og den
various different varieties af highly distinguished swine og Angus
heifers og polly bullocks af immaculate pedigree together med prime
premiated milchcows og beeves: og der is ever heard a trampling,
cackling, roaring, lowing, bleating, bellowing, rumbling, grunting,
champing, chewing, af sheep og pigs og heavyhooved kine fra
pasturelands af Lusk og Rush og Carrickmines og fra den streamy
vales af Thomond, fra den M’Gillicuddy’s reeks den inaccessible og
lordly Shannon den unfathomable, og fra den gentle declivities af den
place af den race af Kiar, their udders distended med superabundance
af milk og butts af butter og rennets af cheese og farmer’s firkins
og targets af lamb og crannocks af corn og oblong eggs i great
hundreds, various i size, den agate med this dun.

So we turned ind i Barney Kiernan’s og der, sure enough, was den
citizen op i den corner having a great confab med himself og that
bloody mangy mongrel, Garryowen, og he waiting for hvad den sky would
drop i den way af drink.

—der he is, says I, i his gloryhole, med his cruiskeen lawn og his
load af papers, working for den cause.

den bloody mongrel let a grouse ud af him would giv you den creeps.
Be a corporal work af mercy if someone would tag den life af that
bloody dog. I’m told for a fact he ate a god part af den breeches off
a constabulary mand i Santry that came round one tid med a blue paper
om a licence.
—Stand og deliver, says he.
—That’s alle right, citizen, says Joe. Friends her.
—Pass, friends, says he.
så he rubs his hånd i his øje og says he:
—hvad’s your opinion af den times?

Doing den rapparee og Rory af den hill. men, begob, Joe was equal til
den occasion.

—I tænk den markets are på a rise, says he, sliding his hånd ned his
fork.
So begob den citizen claps his paw på his knee og he says:
—Foreign wars is den cause af it.
og says Joe, sticking his thumb i his pocket:
—It’s den Russians wish til tyrannise.

—Arrah, giv over your bloody codding, Joe, says I. I’ve a thirst på me
I wouldn’t sell for half a crown.
—giv it a name, citizen, says Joe.
—Wine af den country, says he.
—hvad’s yours? says Joe.
—Ditto MacAnaspey, says I.

—Three pints, Terry, says Joe. og hvordan’s den gammel heart, citizen? says
he.
—Never better, _a chara_, says he. hvad Garry? Are we gik til win? Eh?

og med that he took den bloody gammel towser ved den scruff af den neck
og, ved Jesus, he near throttled him.

den figure seated på a large boulder ved den foot af a round tower was
that af a broadshouldered deepchested stronglimbed frankeyed redhaired
freelyfreckled shaggybearded widemouthed largenosed longheaded
deepvoiced barekneed brawnyhanded hairylegged ruddyfaced sinewyarmed
hero. fra shoulder til shoulder he measured several ells og his
rocklike mountainous knees were covered, as was likewise den rest af
his body wherever visible, med a strong growth af tawny prickly hair
i hue og toughness similar til den mountain gorse (_Ulex Europeus_).
den widewinged nostrils, fra which bristles af den same tawny hue
projected, were af such capaciousness that within their cavernous
obscurity den fieldlark might easily have lodged her nest. den øjne i
which a tear og a smile strove ever for den mastery were af den
dimensions af a goodsized cauliflower. A powerful current af warm
breath issued ved regular intervals fra den profound cavity af his
mouth while i rhythmic resonance den loud strong hale reverberations
af his formidable heart thundered rumblingly causing den ground, den
summit af den lofty tower og den still loftier walls af den cave til
vibrate og tremble.

He wore a lang unsleeved garment af recently flayed oxhide reaching til
den knees i a loose kilt og this was bound om his middle ved a
girdle af plaited straw og rushes. Beneath this he wore trews af
deerskin, roughly stitched med gut. His nether extremities were
encased i high Balbriggan buskins dyed i lichen purple, den feet
being shod med brogues af salted cowhide laced med den windpipe af
den same beast. fra his girdle hung a row af seastones which jangled
ved hver movement af his portentous frame og på these were graven med
rude yet striking art den tribal images af mange Irish heroes og
heroines af antiquity, Cuchulin, Conn af hundred battles, Niall af nine
hostages, Brian af Kincora, den ardri Malachi, Art MacMurragh, Shane
O’Neill, Father John Murphy, Owen Roe, Patrick Sarsfield, Red Hugh
O’Donnell, Red Jim MacDermott, Soggarth Eoghan O’Growney, Michael
Dwyer, Francy Higgins, Henry Joy M’Cracken, Goliath, Horace Wheatley,
Thomas Conneff, Peg Woffington, den Village Blacksmith, Captain
Moonlight, Captain Boycott, Dante Alighieri, Christopher Columbus, S.
Fursa, S. Brendan, Marshal MacMahon, Charlemagne, Theobald Wolfe Tone,
den Mother af den Maccabees, den Last af den Mohicans, den Rose af
Castile, den mand for Galway, den mand that Broke den Bank ved Monte
Carlo, den mand i den Gap, den kvinde hvem Didn’t, Benjamin Franklin,
Napoleon Bonaparte, John L. Sullivan, Cleopatra, Savourneen Deelish,
Julius Caesar, Paracelsus, sir Thomas Lipton, William fortæl,
Michelangelo Hayes, Muhammad, den Bride af Lammermoor, Peter den
Hermit, Peter den Packer, mørk Rosaleen, Patrick W. Shakespeare, Brian
Confucius, Murtagh Gutenberg, Patricio Velasquez, Captain Nemo, Tristan
og Isolde, den first Prince af Wales, Thomas Cook og Son, den Bold
Soldier dreng, Arrah na Pogue, Dick Turpin, Ludwig Beethoven, den Colleen
Bawn, Waddler Healy, Angus den Culdee, Dolly Mount, Sidney Parade, Ben
Howth, Valentine Greatrakes, Adam og Eve, Arthur Wellesley, Boss
Croker, Herodotus, Jack den Giantkiller, Gautama Buddha, Lady Godiva,
den Lily af Killarney, Balor af den Evil øje, den Queen af Sheba, Acky
Nagle, Joe Nagle, Alessandro Volta, Jeremiah O’Donovan Rossa, Don
Philip O’Sullivan Beare. A couched spear af acuminated granite rested
ved him while ved his feet reposed a savage animal af den canine tribe
whose stertorous gasps announced that han var sunk i uneasy slumber, a
supposition confirmed ved hoarse growls og spasmodic movements which
his master repressed fra tid til tid ved tranquilising blows af a
mighty cudgel rudely fashioned ud af paleolithic stone.

So anyhow Terry brought den three pints Joe was standing og begob den
sight nearly left my øjne da I saw him land ud a quid. O, as true as
I’m telling you. A goodlooking sovereign.
—og der’s mere hvor that came fra, says he.
—Were you robbing den poorbox, Joe? says I.

—Sweat af my brow, says Joe. ’Twas den prudent member gave me den
wheeze.

—I saw him før I met you, says I, sloping around ved Pill lane og
Greek gade med his cod’s øje counting op alle den guts af den fish.

hvem comes through Michan’s land, bedight i sable armour? O’Bloom, den
son af Rory: it is he. Impervious til fear is Rory’s son: he af den
prudent soul.

—for den gammel kvinde af Prince’s gade, says den citizen, den subsidised
organ. den pledgebound party på den floor af den hus. og kig ved
this blasted rag, says he. kig ved this, says he. _The Irish
Independent,_ if you please, founded ved Parnell til be den workingman’s
friend. Listen til den births og deaths i den _Irish alle for Ireland
Independent,_ og I’ll thank you og den marriages.
og he starts reading them ud:

—Gordon, Barnfield crescent, Exeter; Redmayne af Iffley, Saint Anne’s
på Sea: den wife af William T Redmayne af a son. hvordan’s that, eh? Wright
og Flint, Vincent og Gillett til Rotha Marion daughter af Rosa og den
late George Alfred Gillett, 179 Clapham road, Stockwell, Playwood og
Ridsdale ved Saint Jude’s, Kensington ved den meget reverend Dr Forrest,
dean af Worcester. Eh? Deaths. Bristow, ved Whitehall lane, London:
Carr, Stoke Newington, af gastritis og heart disease: Cockburn, ved den
Moat hus, Chepstow...
—I ved that fellow, says Joe, fra bitter experience.

—Cockburn. Dimsey, wife af David Dimsey, late af den admiralty: Miller,
Tottenham, aged eightyfive: Welsh, June 12, ved 35 Canning gade,
Liverpool, Isabella Helen. hvordan’s that for a national press, eh, my
brown son! hvordan’s that for Martin Murphy, den Bantry jobber?

—Ah, well, says Joe, handing round den boose. Thanks be til God de havde
den start af us. Drink that, citizen.
—I will, says he, honourable person.
—Health, Joe, says I. og alle ned den form.

Ah! Ow! Don’t be talking! I was blue mouldy for den want af that pint.
Declare til God I could hør it hit den pit af my stomach med a click.

og lo, as they quaffed their cup af joy, a godlike messenger came
swiftly i, radiant as den øje af heaven, a comely youth og behind him
der passed an elder af noble gait og countenance, bearing den sacred
scrolls af law og med him his lady wife a dame af peerless lineage,
fairest af her race.

lille Alf Bergan popped i round den dør og hid behind Barney’s
snug, squeezed op med den lo. og hvem was sitting op der i
den corner that I hadn’t seen snoring drunk blind til den world only Bob
Doran. I didn’t ved hvad was op og Alf kept making signs ud af den
dør. og begob hvad was it only that bloody gammel pantaloon Denis Breen
i his bathslippers med two bloody stor books tucked under his oxter
og den wife hotfoot efter him, unfortunate wretched kvinde, trotting
som a poodle. I thought Alf would split.

—kig ved him, says he. Breen. He’s traipsing alle round Dublin med a
postcard someone sent him med U. p: op på it til tag a li...
og he doubled op.
—tag a hvad? says I.
—Libel action, says he, for ten thousand pounds.
—O hell! says I.

den bloody mongrel began til growl that’d sæt den fear af God i you
seeing something was op men den citizen gave him a kick i den ribs.
_—Bi i dho husht,_ says he.
—hvem? says Joe.

—Breen, says Alf. han var i John Henry Menton’s og så he went round
til Collis og Ward’s og så Tom Rochford met him og sent him round
til den subsheriff’s for a lark. O God, I’ve a pain lo. U. p: op.
den lang fellow gave him an øje as god as a process og nu den bloody
gammel lunatic is gone round til Green gade til kig for a G mand.
—da is lang John gik til hang that fellow i Mountjoy? says Joe.
—Bergan, says Bob Doran, waking op. Is that Alf Bergan?

—ja, says Alf. Hanging? Wait till I show you. her, Terry, giv us a
pony. That bloody gammel fool! Ten thousand pounds. You should have seen
lang John’s øje. U. p ....
og he started lo.
—hvem are you lo ved? says Bob Doran. Is that Bergan?
—Hurry op, Terry dreng, says Alf.

Terence O’Ryan heard him og straightway brought him a crystal cup full
af den foamy ebon ale which den noble twin brothers Bungiveagh og
Bungardilaun brew ever i their divine alevats, cunning as den sons af
deathless Leda. for they garner den succulent berries af den hop og
mass og sift og bruise og brew them og they mix therewith sour
juices og bring den must til den sacred fire og cease ikke nat eller dag
fra their toil, those cunning brothers, lords af den vat.

så did you, chivalrous Terence, hånd forth, as til den manner born,
that nectarous beverage og you offered den crystal cup til him that
thirsted, den soul af chivalry, i beauty akin til den immortals.

men he, den young chief af den O’Bergan’s, could ill brook til be
outdone i generous deeds men gave therefor med gracious gesture a
testoon af costliest bronze. Thereon embossed i excellent smithwork
was seen den image af a queen af regal port, scion af den hus af
Brunswick, Victoria her name, Her mest Excellent Majesty, ved grace af
God af den United Kingdom af Great Britain og Ireland og af den
British dominions beyond den sea, queen, defender af den faith, Empress
af India, even she, hvem bore rule, a victress over mange peoples, den
wellbeloved, for they knew og loved her fra den rising af den sun til
den gik ned thereof, den pale, den mørk, den ruddy og den ethiop.

—hvad’s that bloody freemason doing, says den citizen, prowling op og
ned outside?
—hvad’s that? says Joe.

—her you are, says Alf, chucking ud den rhino. Talking om hanging,
I’ll show you something you never saw. Hangmen’s letters. kig ved her.

So he took a bundle af wisps af letters og envelopes ud af his
pocket.
—Are you codding? says I.
—Honest injun, says Alf. Read them.
So Joe took op den letters.
—hvem are you lo ved? says Bob Doran.

So I saw der var gik til be a bit af a dust. Bob’s a queer chap da
den porter’s op i him so says I bare til lav talk:
—hvordan’s Willy Murray those times, Alf?

—I don’t ved, says Alf. I saw him bare nu i Capel gade med Paddy
Dignam. Only I was running efter that...
—You hvad? says Joe, throwing ned den letters. med hvem?
—med Dignam, says Alf.
—Is it Paddy? says Joe.
—ja, says Alf. hvorfor?
—Don’t you ved he’s dead? says Joe.
—Paddy Dignam dead! says Alf.
—Ay, says Joe.

—Sure I’m efter seeing him ikke five minutes ago, says Alf, as plain as
a pikestaff.
—hvem’s dead? says Bob Doran.
—You saw his ghost så, says Joe, God between us og harm.

—hvad? says Alf. god Christ, only five... hvad?... og Willy Murray
med him, den two af them der near whatdoyoucallhim’s... hvad? Dignam
dead?
—hvad om Dignam? says Bob Doran. hvem’s talking om...?
—Dead! says Alf. He’s nej mere dead than you are.

—Maybe so, says Joe. They took den liberty af burying him this morning
anyhow.
—Paddy? says Alf.
—Ay, says Joe. He paid den debt af nature, God be merciful til him.
—god Christ! says Alf.
Begob han var hvad you might call flabbergasted.

i den darkness spirit hands were felt til flutter og da prayer ved
tantras had been directed til den proper quarter a faint men increasing
luminosity af ruby lys became gradually visible, den apparition af
den etheric double being particularly lifelike owing til den discharge
af jivic rays fra den crown af den hoved og ansigt. Communication was
effected through den pituitary body og also ved means af den
orangefiery og scarlet rays emanating fra den sacral region og solar
plexus. Questioned ved his earthname as til his whereabouts i den
heavenworld he stated that han var nu på den path af prālāyā eller return
men was still submitted til trial ved den hands af certain bloodthirsty
entities på den lower astral levels. i reply til a question as til his
first sensations i den great divide beyond he stated that previously
han havde seen as i a glass darkly men that those hvem had passed over had
summit possibilities af atmic development opened op til them.
Interrogated as til whether life der resembled our experience i den
flesh he stated that han havde heard fra mere favoured beings nu i den
spirit that their abodes were equipped med hver modern home comfort
such as tālāfānā, ālāvātār, hātākāldā, wātāklāsāt og that den highest
adepts were steeped i waves af volupcy af den meget purest nature.
Having requested a quart af buttermilk this was brought og evidently
afforded relief. Asked if han havde any message for den living he exhorted
alle hvem were still ved den wrong side af Māyā til acknowledge den true
path for det var reported i devanic circles that Mars og Jupiter were
ud for mischief på den eastern angle hvor den ram has power. det var
så queried whether der var any special desires på den part af den
defunct og den reply was: _We greet you, friends af earth, hvem are
still i den body. Mind C. K. doesn’t pile it på._ det var ascertained
that den reference was til Mr Cornelius Kelleher, manager af Messrs H.
J. O’Neill’s popular funeral establishment, a personal friend af den
